main_text.p: Apuleio.Apuleius proprium hunc refert Patibuli cruciatum, cum canes & vultures intima protrahunt viscera. Addit autem & Canes: & difcas licet cruces non semper fuisse peraltas. Quomodo enim, si canes attingerent atque etiam lupi? Opinio de Catulliano Epigrammatio.Nam & hos Catullus addit in Epigrammatio, quod mihi quidem non nisi circumlocutio videtur cruciariæ hujus mortis.

p.i: Si Comini arbitrio populi, tua cana fenestus Spurcata impuris moribus, intereat:
Non equidem dubito, quin primum inimica bonorum Lingua exsecta avido sit data vulturio:
Effossos oculos voret atro gutture corvus,

main_text.p: ¹ Lib. vi. De Afin. in fine.

page.notes: Marginal labels "Apu-leio", "Opinio de Catulliano Epigrammatio" are small running side notes, partly damaged. Some words in the verse are uncertain at the page edge; "fenestus" and "vulturio" transcribed as printed. The catchword at the foot is read as "Iftæ" which may be the first word of the following page rather than a catchword; the last line of verse is followed by it.
